skills.name: typescript-development
skills.when: The task creates, modifies, fixes, reviews, refactors, tests, or type-checks TypeScript code, .ts or .tsx files, tsconfig settings, strict types, or typed public APIs.

skills.name: javascript-development
skills.when: The TypeScript task materially involves Node.js or browser runtime behavior, asynchronous I/O, cancellation, error propagation, security, or JavaScript interoperability.

skills.name: react-ui-patterns
skills.when: The TypeScript task builds or reviews React UI state, loading, empty, error, retry, optimistic update, Suspense, or transition behavior.

skills.name: nextjs-development
skills.when: The TypeScript task concerns Next.js routing, Server or Client Components, Server Actions, route handlers, caching, metadata, or deployment boundaries.

skills.name: vue-development
skills.when: The TypeScript task concerns Vue SFCs, script setup, typed props or emits, composables, Pinia, Vue Router, or vue-tsc.

skills.name: frontend-testing
skills.when: The TypeScript work writes or fixes React or general frontend component and hook tests with Vitest, Jest, RTL-style queries, typed fixtures, or typed mocks.

skills.name: vue-testing
skills.when: The TypeScript work writes or fixes Vue component, composable, route, or Pinia tests with Vitest or Vue Test Utils.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.when: A TypeScript compiler, build, module-resolution, inference, narrowing, declaration, or runtime failure has an unknown or disputed cause.

skills.name: code-refactoring
skills.when: The TypeScript change must preserve behavior and public contracts while improving structure or removing unsafe type workarounds.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.when: The TypeScript implementation must proceed through an explicit RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle with a focused regression or contract test.

routingGroups.title: Java Implementation and JVM Specialist Routing
routingGroups.decision: Use java-development as the baseline when Java source, runtime behavior, or public contracts change, then add only the specialist that owns architecture, tests, build tooling, Spring, persistence, debugging, or refactoring. For Maven or Gradle configuration with no Java source or runtime change, use jvm-build-tooling without forcing the Java baseline.

skills.name: java-development
skills.when: The task creates, modifies, fixes, reviews, refactors, tests, or runs Java source, .java files, javac diagnostics, JVM exceptions, concurrency, resources, or Java public APIs.

skills.name: java-architecture
skills.when: The Java task concerns package or module boundaries, Clean Architecture, hexagonal design, DDD, bounded contexts, ports and adapters, or an incremental architecture migration.

skills.name: java-testing
skills.when: The task writes or fixes Java tests, JUnit, Mockito, AssertJ, Testcontainers, ArchUnit, deterministic fixtures, regression coverage, or flaky test behavior.

skills.name: jvm-build-tooling
skills.when: The task concerns Maven, Gradle, wrappers, plugins, dependencies, toolchains, multi-module builds, Java version alignment, or build phases.

skills.name: spring-development
skills.when: The Java task concerns Spring Boot application structure, dependency injection, configuration, controllers, REST APIs, transactions, testing slices, or observability.

skills.name: spring-security
skills.when: The Spring Java task concerns authentication, authorization, OAuth2, OIDC, JWT, CSRF, CORS, method security, filter chains, or security tests.

skills.name: spring-webflux
skills.when: The Java task concerns WebFlux, Reactor, WebClient, R2DBC, reactive pipelines, backpressure, schedulers, cancellation, WebTestClient, or StepVerifier.

skills.name: spring-cloud-microservices
skills.when: The Java task concerns Spring Cloud, service boundaries, gateways, Kafka, distributed events, resilience, tracing, or service-to-service communication.

skills.name: jpa-hibernate-development
skills.when: The Java task concerns JPA, Hibernate, Spring Data, entities, repositories, ORM transactions, fetching, N plus 1 queries, projections, or persistence tests.

skills.name: mybatis-development
skills.when: The Java task concerns MyBatis mapper interfaces, XML, bindings, ResultMap definitions, dynamic SQL, batch execution, or MyBatis transactions.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.when: A Java compiler, build, test, exception, concurrency, resource, JVM runtime, or framework failure has an unknown or disputed cause.

skills.name: code-refactoring
skills.when: The Java change must preserve behavior and public contracts while improving structure, naming, duplication, or maintainability.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.when: The Java implementation must proceed through an explicit RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle with a focused regression or contract test.

routingGroups.title: Native iOS Architecture and Delivery
routingGroups.decision: Choose by concern: app and module boundaries, SwiftUI implementation, concurrency and isolation, code-level testing, device behavior, or release readiness.

skills.name: ios-architecture
skills.when: The task is selecting or reviewing Swift app architecture, feature and module boundaries, dependency direction, state and effect ownership, navigation ownership, or an incremental migration.

skills.name: swiftui-development
skills.when: The task is implementing or reviewing SwiftUI state, views, identity, navigation, lifecycle-safe concurrency, accessibility, compatibility, or rendering performance.

skills.name: swift-concurrency
skills.when: The task is diagnosing actor-isolation or Sendable diagnostics, designing task lifetime or cancellation, adopting async/await, actors, or AsyncSequence, or migrating targets to Swift 6 strict concurrency.

skills.name: swift-testing
skills.when: The task is writing or reviewing native Swift unit and integration tests, using Swift Testing APIs, testing async or actor-isolated code, fixing parallel-test flakiness, or migrating XCTest.

skills.name: mobile-app-testing
skills.when: The task is proving behavior across devices, simulators, lifecycle events, permissions, offline states, deep links, push notifications, purchases, or mobile automation.

skills.name: app-store-release
skills.when: The implementation is ready for signing, archive validation, privacy declarations, TestFlight, App Store metadata, review, or staged release.

routingGroups.title: Testing and Quality Lifecycle
routingGroups.decision: Choose by test lifecycle stage, target layer, and required evidence rather than by test tool name alone.

skills.name: testing-strategy
skills.when: The task is choosing test levels, confidence targets, fixture strategy, coverage boundaries, and maintenance tradeoffs.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.when: New or changed behavior should be implemented through a strict red-green-refactor cycle.

skills.name: swift-testing
skills.when: The task is native Swift unit or integration testing with Swift Testing or XCTest, including parameterized cases, traits, async behavior, parallel isolation, or framework migration.

skills.name: frontend-testing
skills.when: React or TypeScript units, hooks, components, or RTL-style behavior need focused non-browser tests.

skills.name: e2e-testing-patterns
skills.when: The task is designing and maintaining reliable browser E2E suites, fixtures, critical flows, CI integration, or flake control.

skills.name: playwright-automation
skills.when: The task explicitly requires Playwright locators, traces, scripted interactions, screenshots, or browser automation.

skills.name: webapp-testing
skills.when: A local web application needs outcome-focused functional verification, UI troubleshooting, screenshots, and browser-log checks.

skills.name: accessibility-testing
skills.when: The interface needs WCAG, keyboard, focus, screen-reader, reflow, contrast, or reduced-motion evidence.

skills.name: visual-regression-testing
skills.when: Visual fidelity, screenshots, baselines, OCR, DOM geometry, or machine acceptance gates are the primary evidence.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.when: A regression or failure exists but its root cause is not understood and hypotheses must be tested before changing code.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.when: Implementation is believed complete and fresh commands, behavior checks, diff inspection, and repository state must prove it.

routingGroups.title: Skill Discovery, Review, and Release
routingGroups.decision: Choose one owner by the artifact needed now: cross-tool contract, local route, external gap decision, CLI action, read-only scan, deterministic lint, semantic audit, focused security decision, controlled runtime proof, or versioned release evidence.

skills.name: skill-creator-design
skills.when: A new or materially redesigned cross-tool Skill needs ownership, invocation, completion, residue, resources, and platform-creator handoffs defined before implementation.

skills.name: skill-explorer
skills.when: The user needs to navigate the local catalog, compare nearby Skills, or select the smallest useful local route.

skills.name: skill-gap-analyzer
skills.when: Local coverage must be compared with marketplaces or GitHub to decide whether to upgrade, add, or keep unchanged.

skills.name: skillctl
skills.when: The exact source, target, scope, and owner are known and the task is a direct query, install, update, use, initialization, or supported removal command.

skills.name: skill-scan
skills.when: An unfamiliar Skill folder needs a deterministic read-only inventory, hashes, executable surfaces, and suspicious-pattern triage before deeper checks.

skills.name: skill-lint
skills.when: SKILL.md structure, frontmatter, naming, links, package shape, eval schema, provenance locks, or repository-native deterministic gates must be validated.

skills.name: skill-audit
skills.when: Invocation fit, semantic completeness, evidence, overlap, provenance, maintenance, and overall package risk need review.

skills.name: skill-security-review
skills.when: A third-party or executable Skill needs focused supply-chain, permissions, secrets, data-flow, network, and prompt-injection review.

skills.name: skill-executor
skills.when: Static review cannot prove behavior and a Skill needs an explicit isolation packet, controlled execution, repeated-run evidence, side-effect observation, and cleanup proof.

skills.name: skillforge
skills.when: A frozen Skill revision needs candidate-versus-baseline evaluation, held-out thresholds, runtime and safety evidence, an unsigned manifest, approval, and optional approved attestation.

routingGroups.title: Video Production Stage and Medium
routingGroups.decision: Use the production workflow as orchestrator, then select specialists by artifact stage, generation method, or final format.

skills.name: video-production-workflow
skills.when: A complete video project needs coordinated brief, treatment, script, storyboard, continuity, assets, edit, review, and approval gates.

skills.name: storyboard-creation
skills.when: A script or idea must become scenes, shots, timing, camera notes, dialogue, and production-ready shot tables.

skills.name: short-video-script
skills.when: The deliverable is a short-form TikTok, Reels, Shorts, Douyin, or Xiaohongshu script with hook, pacing, and CTA.

skills.name: vlog-production
skills.when: The project is a vlog requiring story arc, footage review, talking-head beats, B-roll, edit, packaging, and repurposing.

skills.name: ugc-video-ads
skills.when: The deliverable is a creator-style product ad with persona, hook, demo, objections, social proof, and platform variants.

skills.name: ai-video-generation
skills.when: New clips must be generated through text-to-video, image-to-video, or reference-driven AI video providers.

skills.name: avatar-video-generation
skills.when: The output is a presenter, talking-head, digital-human, avatar, or lip-synced video.

skills.name: remotion-video-toolkit
skills.when: The output should be deterministic, programmable, data-driven, and rendered through React and Remotion.

skills.name: video-edit
skills.when: Existing media must be trimmed, concatenated, resized, compressed, converted, inspected, or edited with local tools.

skills.name: subtitle-captions
skills.when: The task is subtitle timing, caption formatting, SRT/VTT production, readability, or caption accessibility.

routingGroups.title: Writing Artifact and Transformation
routingGroups.decision: Choose by target artifact and transformation intent; do not apply generic polishing when a specialist must preserve evidence or structure.

skills.name: answer-writing
skills.when: The target is a concise, actionable final response to a user.

skills.name: humanizer
skills.when: Existing text is correct but sounds stiff, repetitive, promotional, formulaic, or obviously AI-generated.

skills.name: brand-voice
skills.when: Writing must extract, document, or consistently apply a specific organization, publication, product, or creator voice.

skills.name: product-pitch-writing
skills.when: Verified product or system truth must become audience-specific selling points, a timed presentation speech, demo narrative, keynote, or speaker notes.

skills.name: article-writing
skills.when: The deliverable is an evidence-led long-form article, guide, essay, or newsletter.

skills.name: content-repurposing
skills.when: One approved source must become multiple channel-specific derivatives without introducing unsupported claims.

skills.name: ux-writing
skills.when: The text is interface microcopy such as labels, errors, empty states, onboarding, notifications, or form help.

skills.name: markdown-writer
skills.when: The main requirement is clear GFM structure, headings, tables, examples, and general Markdown documentation.

skills.name: git-readme-writer
skills.when: A repository README must be derived from actual project structure, setup, usage, architecture, and contribution paths.

skills.name: specification-authoring
skills.when: A formal technical specification with prescribed structure, numbering, diagrams, traceability, and version history is required.

routingGroups.title: Code Review Scope and Ownership
routingGroups.decision: Use code-review as the risk profile, evidence, severity, coverage, and verdict umbrella for bounded change review; add or substitute the narrow specialist according to review context, domain, and whether the task is analysis, publication, remediation, or a repeatable gate.

skills.name: code-review
skills.when: A bounded diff, commit, branch comparison, changed file, working tree, or pasted snippet needs a risk-calibrated read-only review with intent and implementation passes, concrete findings, honest coverage, and a verdict.

skills.name: frontend-code-review
skills.when: The change affects frontend state, rendering, accessibility, responsiveness, browser behavior, CSS, React, TypeScript, or user-visible UI logic.

skills.name: security-code-review
skills.when: The primary question is vulnerability, exploitability, attacker control, trust boundaries, authentication, authorization, injection, secrets, cryptography, infrastructure security, or validation of a potentially blocking security finding.

skills.name: github-code-review
skills.when: An existing GitHub pull request needs a first review or re-review using frozen base and head SHAs, merge-base diff, commits, prior findings, comments, changed files, and checks.

skills.name: github-inline-review
skills.when: Existing review findings must be published as GitHub inline comments, suggestion blocks, approval, comment, or request-changes actions after explicit authorization.

skills.name: project-architecture-review
skills.when: The requested review concerns repository-wide architecture, module boundaries, dependency direction, data flow, or restructuring options rather than one bounded change.

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.when: Review findings already exist and must be validated, disputed, accepted, implemented, tested, and returned for re-review.

skills.name: pipeline-review
skills.when: A completed stage needs an independent repeatable review gate with risk-calibrated depth, stable finding IDs, coverage, verification gaps, ownership, and re-review loops.

routingGroups.title: Git and GitHub Operation Boundary
routingGroups.decision: Choose first between local Git and remote GitHub, then between analysis-only and state-changing operations.

skills.name: git-operations
skills.when: The task is routine local repository status, branch, stage, commit, pull, push, merge, rebase, stash, or conflict handling.

skills.name: git-advanced
skills.when: The task needs worktrees, bisect, interactive rebase, recovery, hooks, history repair, or advanced Git control.

skills.name: github-operations
skills.when: The task concerns remote issues, pull requests, releases, checks, workflow runs, or GitHub API operations.

skills.name: github-code-review
skills.when: An existing GitHub pull request needs a read-only first review or re-review with frozen revisions, prior-finding disposition, diff, discussion, and check analysis.

skills.name: github-inline-review
skills.when: Review findings must be submitted as line-level comments, suggestion blocks, approval, comment, or request-changes actions.

skills.name: github-actions-ci
skills.when: The task is specifically creating, debugging, or reviewing GitHub Actions workflow YAML, jobs, matrices, caching, or permissions.

routingGroups.title: Web Extraction, Browser Control, and Browser QA
routingGroups.decision: Choose by page type and intent: static extraction, interactive automation, tool-specific scripting, diagnostics, local verification, or specialized QA.

skills.name: python-web-scraping
skills.when: Content can be collected through HTTP and parsed from static or lightly dynamic HTML without driving a real browser.

skills.name: browser-automation
skills.when: A real browser must navigate, click, fill forms, capture screenshots, extract rendered data, or repeat web interactions.

skills.name: playwright-automation
skills.when: The browser task explicitly requires Playwright locators, traces, scripted flows, MCP, or CLI execution.

skills.name: chrome-devtools-debugging
skills.when: The goal is diagnosing console, network, runtime, performance, DOM, accessibility tree, storage, or page-load behavior.

skills.name: webapp-testing
skills.when: A local web application needs functional validation and UI troubleshooting rather than general web automation.

skills.name: e2e-testing-patterns
skills.when: The work concerns E2E suite architecture, critical-flow selection, fixtures, flakiness, maintenance, or CI.

skills.name: browser-compatibility-testing
skills.when: The risk is differences across Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, mobile browsers, or remote browser grids.

skills.name: visual-regression-testing
skills.when: The browser output must be compared against approved visual baselines or machine-readable fidelity criteria.

skills.name: agent-reach-ops
skills.when: Evidence must retain native social, video, podcast, code-hosting, or RSS authorship, timestamps, transcript provenance, revision state, and source lineage.

skills.name: web-research-ops
skills.when: The main outcome is verified research with source quality and citations rather than extraction automation itself.

routingGroups.title: Planning, Discovery, and Delivery Stage
routingGroups.decision: Choose by lifecycle stage and task duration: clarify, discover, prototype, specify, plan, edit, slice, hand off, or verify.

skills.name: ask-questions-if-underspecified
skills.when: The user explicitly requests a question-first approach and only the minimum missing information is needed.

skills.name: requirements-deep-dive
skills.when: The user explicitly requests a deliberate one-decision-at-a-time interview that challenges assumptions and records decisions.

skills.name: solution-discovery
skills.when: The outcome is known but solution direction, alternatives, scope, or architecture tradeoffs are not yet approved.

skills.name: throwaway-prototyping
skills.when: One unresolved product, interaction, visual, logic, architecture, or integration question needs disposable executable evidence.

skills.name: spec-flow
skills.when: Requirements or direction are clear and must become acceptance criteria, vertical slices, dependencies, and executable work items.

skills.name: todo-first
skills.when: The current task has several meaningful steps and needs runtime-neutral progress tracking in this session.

skills.name: code-change-workflow
skills.when: Existing code will change and entry points, call chains, data flow, tests, constraints, and verification paths must be inspected first.

skills.name: incremental-implementation
skills.when: A large change must be divided into small verified slices, checkpoints, reviewable commits, or rollback-safe stages.

skills.name: multi-session-planning
skills.when: The work spans sessions, agents, tools, milestones, or context windows and needs a durable dependency and ownership map.

skills.name: session-handoff
skills.when: Non-trivial work must pause, transfer ownership, cross a context boundary, or resume from an evidence-linked handoff.

skills.name: verified-software-delivery
skills.when: The whole delivery chain from approved problem framing through implementation, review, and completion needs orchestration.

routingGroups.title: Security Analysis Scope and Evidence
routingGroups.decision: Choose by whether the task starts from an architecture, an unknown codebase risk, a known vulnerability family, an operationalized detector, or a binary artifact.

skills.name: threat-modeling
skills.when: Assets, trust boundaries, attacker capabilities, abuse cases, or required security invariants are not yet explicit.

skills.name: security-code-review
skills.when: A code change or component needs a first-pass vulnerability review without a confirmed seed family.

skills.name: vulnerability-variant-analysis
skills.when: A credible known issue, incomplete fix, or recurring weakness should be expanded into a root-cause predicate and complete variant ledger.

skills.name: security-scanning
skills.when: A mature, tested rule or scanner must be configured, automated, triaged, and enforced in delivery workflows.

skills.name: reverse-engineering
skills.when: The authorized evidence is a binary, firmware image, protocol, memory artifact, or undocumented implementation rather than source code.

routingGroups.title: Product Research and Experimentation Method
routingGroups.decision: Choose by the uncertainty and evidence needed: market context, user behavior, design precedents, solution direction, controlled optimization, or causal product impact.

skills.name: market-research
skills.when: The decision needs evidence about markets, competitors, positioning, demand, or external alternatives.

skills.name: ux-research
skills.when: The uncertainty concerns real user needs, behavior, comprehension, accessibility, or why a workflow succeeds or fails.

skills.name: design-intelligence-search
skills.when: The task needs searchable design precedents, patterns, visual directions, or accessibility references before a design decision.

skills.name: solution-discovery
skills.when: The outcome is known but viable approaches, trade-offs, scope, or implementation direction are not yet approved.

skills.name: autoresearch
skills.when: A measurable artifact or system can be improved through controlled, repeatable optimization loops with a fixed evaluator.

skills.name: product-experimentation
skills.when: A causal product decision can be tested through randomized assignment, predeclared metrics, instrumentation checks, and a ship-or-stop rule.
